ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: The figure is a green triangle. Its upper-right slanted side is labeled 26 yd, the base is labeled 16 yd, and the left slanted side is not directly labeled. Outside the left side of the triangle there is a right triangle formed by a set of pink dashed lines; the vertical dashed side is labeled 10 yd, and the horizontal dashed side is labeled 8 yd; these two dashed sides correspond to the horizontal and vertical distances of the unlabeled left slanted side. Then reason: To find the perimeter of the green triangle, the lengths of three sides are needed. The two known sides are 26 yd and 16 yd. The unlabeled left slanted side can be found from the pink dashed right triangle using the Pythagorean theorem: left slanted side = sqrt(10^2 + 8^2) = sqrt(100 + 64) = sqrt(164) ≈ 12.806. Perimeter = 26 + 16 + sqrt(164) ≈ 26 + 16 + 12.806 = 54.806, which rounded to the nearest tenth is 54.8 yd.

method.method_draft: Read the image as a green triangular figure whose boundary sides are the slanted top/right side labeled 26 yd, the bottom side labeled 16 yd, and an unlabeled left slanted side. Also read the dashed magenta right triangle outside the figure: vertical leg 10 yd and horizontal leg 8 yd connect the top vertex to the left base vertex. Use the Pythagorean theorem on this dashed right triangle to find the missing left boundary side: sqrt(10^2+8^2). Then add the three boundary lengths: 26 + 16 + sqrt(164), and round to the nearest tenth.
